scope_note: Family-recognition backfill using the 18 Onagraceae rows in the Master Plant Pool. All current pool taxa are placed in Oenothera, including taxa formerly treated in Gaura. Existing B003 species decisions are preserved.

pool_taxa: Oenothera macrocarpa subsp./var. missouriensis source row
local_scope.range_guardrail: Oenothera lindheimeri remains canonical only under the existing user-approved range exception. Its current authoritative native range is southeastern Texas to southwestern Louisiana, and Central Texas occurrences must not be represented as proof of native target-zone status.

family_lesson.where_to_look_first: Look below the petals. In the local Oenothera, the ovary sits below the sepals/petals/stamens, so the flower appears to rise from the top of an inferior ovary, often through an obvious floral tube/hypanthium. Then confirm the repeated 4-part architecture: commonly 4 sepals, 4 petals, 4 or 8 stamens, and a 4-lobed stigma.
family_lesson.strongest_field_confirmation: Inferior ovary + hypanthium/floral tube + usually 4-part flower + 4-lobed stigma. Fruit then tells you which Oenothera form you are dealing with.
core_characters: Mostly herbs in the local flora; leaves simple, alternate and often rosetted basally; stipules absent in Oenothera.
Flowers bisexual, radial in classic evening-primrose forms or strongly bilateral/zygomorphic in many former-Gaura forms.
Hypanthium/floral tube commonly conspicuous above the ovary.
Sepals usually 4 and petals usually 4 in the local Oenothera; petals are free rather than fused.
Stamens commonly 8, but local Oenothera triloba is a useful 4-stamen exception.
Pollen in Onagraceae is often linked by viscin threads; this is a technical microscopy/macro character rather than a first field cue.
Ovary inferior, usually 4-carpellate/4-loculed in the local teaching set.
Style one; stigma commonly deeply 4-lobed in Oenothera.
Fruit may be a many-seeded dehiscent capsule OR a hard few-seeded indehiscent/nutlike capsule in the former-Gaura lineage.
avoid_overgeneralizing: Do not teach Onagraceae as 'yellow evening primrose.' Local flowers can be yellow, pink, white or white fading pink/red.
Do not teach the flowers as always radial. Former-Gaura Oenothera such as O. lindheimeri can be strongly zygomorphic with petals held to one side.
Do not teach '8 stamens' as absolute. Oenothera triloba has 4 stamens in the Williamson County treatment.
Do not teach the fruit as always an opening many-seeded capsule. Oenothera sect. Gaura has woody indehiscent nutlike capsules with few seeds.
Do not use flower color as the family diagnostic; the inferior ovary + floral tube + 4-part reproductive architecture is far more reliable.

classic_primrose_form.pattern: Usually conspicuous radial 4-petaled flower; long or short floral tube; 4-lobed stigma; fruit often a many-seeded dehiscent capsule.
classic_primrose_form.teaching_value: Shows the classic Onagraceae architecture clearly.

former_gaura_form.pattern: Flowers arranged along spikes/racemes, sometimes strongly zygomorphic with exserted stamens; fruit often hard, few-seeded and indehiscent.
former_gaura_form.teaching_value: Prevents the learner from thinking all Oenothera look like large evening primroses.

Lythraceae.confusion: Both can have 4-merous flowers and a hypanthium/floral cup.
Lythraceae.tie_breaker: Onagraceae has an inferior ovary. Kew specifically separates Lythraceae by its usually superior ovary; inspect where the sepals/petals/stamens attach relative to the ovary.

Cistaceae.confusion: Some showy herbs have free petals and a superficially similar open flower.
Cistaceae.tie_breaker: Cistaceae usually has 5 petals, numerous stamens and a superior ovary; local Oenothera is commonly 4-petaled with 4 or 8 stamens and an inferior ovary/floral tube.

other 4-petaled herbs.confusion: Petal count alone can send the learner toward Brassicaceae or other unrelated families.
other 4-petaled herbs.tie_breaker: Find the inferior ovary and hypanthium first; petal number is only supporting evidence.

fast_key: Flower seems to sit on top of a green ovary, often with a tube between ovary and petals → strong Onagraceae clue.
Large radial 4-petaled flower + obvious 4-lobed stigma + many-seeded capsule → classic Oenothera form.
Wandlike spike/raceme + small or one-sided 4-petaled flowers + long exserted stamens + hard few-seeded fruit → former-Gaura Oenothera form.
4-petaled flower but ovary clearly superior → reconsider Lythraceae, Cistaceae or another family.

anchor_cards.look_here_first: Large open radial flower with 4 broad pink/white petals, 8 stamens and a conspicuous 4-lobed stigma; the green inferior ovary lies below the floral tube.
confirms: Hypanthium 10–15 mm above the inferior ovary.
Four sepals and four broad petals.
